label: early-sequence conjunction: first copy step after "1 ... l" starts, or step 2 after "[l/x/3/d] i"
predicate: ((recall_idx == 1) & (in_tok == tok("1")) & ((orig(1) == tok("l")) | (orig(2) == tok("l")) | (orig(3) == tok("l")))) | ((t == 2) & (prev_tok == tok("i")) & isin(prev2_tok, [tok("l"), tok("x"), tok("3"), tok("d")]))
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.04% of steps) with two main contexts, both near the start of a sequence. (A) about 54% of mass: the first copy step (t = L+1, re-inputting orig(0)), strongest when orig(0) is the digit 1 and an l comes soon after (orig 1-3). The top activations (~0.2-0.24) are all of the form "1 l l ..." / "1 3 l l" / "1 r l". It sometimes also fires weakly with other first tokens (f, r, n) when an l follows. (B) about 33% of mass: original step t=2 when the previous token is i and the token before that is l/x/3/d ("l i _", "x i _"), at moderate strength (~0.1-0.13). The rest is weak firing at steps 3-8 in sequences with l/3 among the early tokens. It never fires at t=0/1, at recall_idx >= 3, or after the copy goes wrong. Precision is low (~0.27) because these token conjunctions are necessary-ish but not sufficient, so the predicate captures only about 44% of the mass. The feature looks like a conjunctive detector for a specific early hidden-state content (a 1/l/i combination) rather than a clean concept.
